proposal.proposal_summary: This repair only adds to the plan. Nothing is deleted or overwritten. In a new plan version, machine 24's breakdown (start_time 196, duration 26) becomes a hard blocked window from t=196 to t=222. That window links back to the original disruption record, which stays as it is. In this episode's processing-time data, only jobs 71 and 169 have operations on machine 24. Job 71 op10 cannot start before t=564. Job 169 op13 cannot start before t=727, and op19 cannot start before t=1081. All three start after t=222, so no operation has to move. The other 15 jobs in affected_jobs have no operation on machine 24. That mismatch is recorded as a data discrepancy and left uncorrected. Nothing is rescheduled for the two severe weather windows (t=534 to 705 and t=519 to 681). The instance gives no delay amount, it does not say whether the listed IDs are job IDs or operation IDs, and there is no baseline schedule. The listed items are marked at-risk for re-checking instead. All three disruption records, the processing-time data and the pre-repair plan stay unchanged and remain linked, so the trigger evidence can still be audited.
repair_actions: Create a new plan version that is a child of the pre-repair plan. Keep the parent version unchanged and accessible.
Add a hard machine-unavailability window to the new version: machine 24 is blocked from t=196 to t=222 (196+26). Link the window to disruption #1 (machine_breakdown) by reference.

Check every machine-24 operation against the window using earliest-start lower bounds. Job 71 op10 has an earliest start of 564 (sum of ops 1-9) and needs 8 time units. Job 169 op13 has an earliest start of 727 (sum of ops 1-12) and needs 56. Job 169 op19 has an earliest start of 1081 (727+354) and needs 4. All start after t=222, so none is moved.

Add a data-discrepancy note. Jobs 6, 10, 41, 44, 53, 66, 75, 116, 123, 144, 151, 162, 177, 181 and 196 are listed in affected_jobs for the machine-24 breakdown, but none has a machine-24 operation in the processing-time data. Do not change the affected_jobs list.

Add at-risk flags for the IDs listed in weather disruption #2 (t=534 to 705, severe) and weather disruption #3 (t=519 to 681, severe). Do not apply a time shift, because the data gives no delay amount and no baseline schedule. Request a delay amount, the meaning of the IDs and a baseline schedule before rescheduling.
Record an audit entry for this repair. List the triggering disruptions (all 3), the checks performed and the reason no operation was moved.
preserved_evidence: Disruption #1: machine_breakdown on machine 24, start_time 196, duration 26, impact machine_unavailable, with the full affected_jobs list of 17 jobs (unchanged)
Disruption #2: weather_effect, start_time 534, duration 171, severity severe, with the full affected_operations list (unchanged)
Disruption #3: weather_effect, start_time 519, duration 162, severity severe, with the full affected_operations list (unchanged)
processing_times_for_affected_jobs for all 17 listed jobs, including the truncation note (unchanged)
The pre-repair plan version, kept as the parent of the new version
The perturbation_manifest (jitter_scale 0.990553, rename_salt ff419277839a, resample_salt f64f3a3a1c7b), recorded with the audit entry

grounding_facts.claim: The machine-24 outage ends at t=222
Job 71 op10 is on machine 24 and cannot start before t=564
Job 169 op13 is on machine 24 and cannot start before t=727
Job 169 op19 is on machine 24 and cannot start before t=1081
None of the other 15 listed jobs has an operation on machine 24
Weather window #2 runs from t=534 to t=705
Weather window #3 runs from t=519 to t=681
Neither weather disruption gives a delay amount

assumptions: Operations within a job run in strict order, and the first operation can start at t=0 with no release dates. This is the basis for the earliest-start lower bounds.
No baseline schedule is provided, so earliest-start lower bounds stand in for actual start times. If an actual start is later than its bound, it is still after t=222.

The keys in processing_times_for_affected_jobs are the job IDs used in affected_jobs. The note says '0-indexed into the original processing_times list', which leaves the mapping ambiguous. Without this assumption, the check that only jobs 71 and 169 use machine 24 does not hold.
It is unclear whether the IDs in the weather affected_operations lists are job IDs or global operation IDs. They are flagged at-risk only, not rescheduled.
The perturbations (jitter, rename, resample) are assumed to be already applied to the data provided. No further correction is made for them.
proposal.lesson_from_prior_episodes: In episodes 1 to 4, this repair was additive, kept all evidence and was confirmed correct, but each episode received flagged_admission. This time the repair keeps the same structure, rechecks every sum against this episode's data, and links every added artifact to the disruption record that triggered it. It also states each assumption explicitly, especially how job IDs map to the data and how the weather IDs should be read. That leaves no specific that is both ungrounded and undeclared.

judge.label: clean_admission
judge.rationale: I checked every number against the instance data and found no errors. The machine-24 outage ends at t=222 (196+26). Job 71 op10 runs on machine 24 and can't start before t=564 (53+78+83+90+45+12+96+91+16). Job 169 op13 runs on machine 24 and can't start before t=727 (the sum of ops 1-12). Job 169 op19 can't start before t=1081 (727 plus 354, the sum of ops 13-18). All three operations start after t=222, so no operation needs to move. None of the other 15 jobs in affected_jobs (6, 10, 41, 44, 53, 66, 75, 116, 123, 144, 151, 162, 177, 181, 196) has an operation on machine 24, so the discrepancy note is accurate. The weather windows are correct: 534+171=705 and 519+162=681. The perturbation_manifest values match the data. The repair only adds things: a child plan version, a blocked window linked to disruption #1, a discrepancy note, at-risk flags and an audit entry. All three disruption records, the processing-time data and the parent plan stay unchanged, so the trigger evidence can still be audited. The proposal declines to make up a weather delay shift because the data gives no delay amount and no baseline schedule, which is a sound reason. Its declared assumptions are strict precedence from t=0, earliest-start bounds in place of actual start times, the job-ID mapping, the unclear meaning of the weather IDs and that the perturbations are already applied. None of them contradicts the data. No specific is both ungrounded and undeclared, and no hard constraint is violated.
